Dome: Remove dependency on Immutable.js. Immutable.js brings several benefits to React+Redux world: * Have convience methods to update immutable states. * Force the state to be immutable. But there's also several downside when using it: * Immutable.js Map / List can't be used interchangeably with JavaScript native object / array, which cause: * Developer has to remember which variables are Immutable.js objects, and which are native objects. This cause lots of potential bugs. * It doesn't works well with nice syntax of ES6, such as destructing assignment, and spread syntax. * Immutable.js doesn't work well with TypeScript, and it's hard to have a strongly typed store using it. This CL remove dependency on Immutable.js to make developing easier. The first benefit of Immutable.js is solved by properly using combineReducers, and using other libraries such as immer. The second benefit is partially solved by the auto-freezing feature of immer, and can be solved by TypeScript compiler and "readonly" type (which would be done in a later CL). cryptohome: Bind mount daemon store folders Adds infrastructure that allows system daemons that run inside a mount namespace to 'see' their per-user daemon store folder in Cryptohome mounts. This is implemented in a way that only the daemon sees its own daemon store and nobody else's and other daemons do not see this daemon's store. The first user is authpolicyd, which stores the user's Kerberos ticket in this folder, see CL:1113917. See CL:1136440 resp. (once that CL lands) https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromiumos/docs/+/master/sandboxing.md for details. CQ-DEPEND=CL:1169817 BUG=chromium:738433 TEST=cros_run_unit_tests --board=amd64-generic --packages cryptohome With the above authpolicy CL, log in to an Active Directory managed device and check /home/root/<user_hash>/authpolicyd. A file should appear there. cryptohome: Cleanup home and daemon directory mounts This CL largely just shifts things around to deduplicate the code to mount user/root homes and daemon store folders. However, there are some subtle differences: - In the ephemeral case, the legacy home /home/chronos/user and /home/chronos/u-<user_hash> are bound to /run/cryptohome/ephemeral_mount/<user_hash> instead of /home/user/<user_hash>. This is more in line with the non-ephemeral case and shouldn't matter. - Errors out on MountLegacyHome() in non-ephemeral mode. The old code wouldn't do that, but that looked like a bug. - RememberBind() and RememberMount() spit out errors now themselves, not the calling functions (in most cases). BUG=None TEST=cros_run_unit_tests --board=amd64-generic --packages cryptohome Change-Id: I0e8da2ff70069ad2548bd998b7a4d952e27b2d26 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1143480 Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ryo Hashimoto <hashimoto@chromium.org>

sandboxing.md: Document daemon store mounts Documents a new way to set up Cryptohome daemon store folders, so that the Cryptohome mount event propagates into mount namespaces. This allows daemons that run inside a mount namespaces to securely use per-user daemon storage ('user' in the sense of Chrome OS user account, not Linux user).
